title: Formal functions over a Noetherian affine base for algebraic spaces
statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-affine-spectrum, lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. Let $F$ be a coherent module on $X$. Coherent means quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and, on an affine etale cover by spectra of Noetherian rings, associated to finitely generated modules [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. All module sheaves, tensor pullbacks and direct images are on the small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]; $R^qf_*$ and $H^q$ are computed by injective resolutions in all structure-sheaf module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For $n\geq1$ put $X_n=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^n)$, with projection $j_n:X_n\to X$, and put $F_n=j_n^*F$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For every $q\geq0$, the canonical restriction maps $H^q(X,F)\to H^q(X_n,F_n)$ vanish on $I^nH^q(X,F)$ and induce a compatible system
$$\theta_n:H^q(X,F)/I^nH^q(X,F)\longrightarrow H^q(X_n,F_n).$$
Their inverse limit is an isomorphism of $\widehat A$-modules
$$\varprojlim_n\theta_n:\widehat{H^q(X,F)}\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{n\geq1}H^q(X_n,F_n),\qquad \widehat A=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/I^n,$$
where $\widehat{H^q(X,F)}=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}H^q(X,F)/I^nH^q(X,F)$ is the $I$-adic completion of the $A$-module $H^q(X,F)$, with the transition maps induced by $I^{n+1}H^q(X,F)\subseteq I^nH^q(X,F)$ and $\widehat A$ acting coordinatewise, and $\widehat A$ is the $I$-adic completion of [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Transitions on the right are restriction along $X_n\hookrightarrow X_{n+1}$ and the canonical tensor identification $F_{n+1}|_{X_n}\simeq F_n$; scalar multiplication by $(a_n)_n\in\widehat A$ acts coordinatewise by $a_n$. The comparison is natural in $F$. No completeness or locality assumption on $A$, and no flatness assumption on $F$ or $f$, is imposed.

proof.text: Every affine etale chart of $X$ is locally of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, by the chart definition of finite type for the proper map. Since the base is locally Noetherian, pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft makes these charts locally Noetherian. Thus $X$ is locally Noetherian. The cover form of coherence in the statement gives the every-chart form used by the cited nodes: for an affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, with $F$ given there by an $R$-module $N$, cover $\operatorname{Spec}R\times_X U_i$ by finitely many affines $\operatorname{Spec}C_k$ etale over the cover's Noetherian spectra $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$; there $C_k\otimes_RN\cong C_k\otimes_{B_i}P_i$ is finitely generated, so $N$ is finitely generated over $R$ by lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-descent-finite-module applied to the faithfully flat $R\to\prod_kC_k$, and hence coherent on the Noetherian $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Set $J=I\mathcal O_X$, $G_n=J^nF$ and $Q_n=F/G_n$. Choose finitely many generators of $I^n$, possible since $A$ is Noetherian. The corresponding map $F^{\oplus t}\to F$ has image $G_n$, because products in $J$ expand into products of elements of $I$. By lem-sfb-space-coherent-abelian, its kernel and then its image (the cokernel of the kernel inclusion) are coherent, as is $Q_n$. The same argument covers $n=0$ with $G_0=F$. Also $I^nQ_n=0$, directly from the quotient.

proof.text: Use lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model to replace each space's small ringed etale site by the equivalent enlarged site with the space itself terminal. An equivalence transports the lifting property for injectives, exact sequences, and global sections. The nonnegative module injective resolutions of lem-sfb-module-resolution-derived-presheaf-comparison exist there. At the terminal object, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison identifies their cohomology naturally with additive sheaf cohomology, identically in degree zero. Applying naturality to each scalar endomorphism gives the same $A$-action. We can therefore use both the additive cohomology assertions below and the specified module-resolution convention. Derived global sections, with the $A$-action from $f$, is an additive left exact functor into $A$-modules; lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor supplies its $A$-linear long exact sequences, natural in short exact sequences.

proof.text: The base change $j_n$ is a representable closed immersion: on an affine scheme chart $\operatorname{Spec}B\to X$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/I^nB)\to\operatorname{Spec}B$. In particular it is affine. On that chart, if $F$ corresponds to $P$, its tensor pullback corresponds to $(B/I^nB)\otimes_BP=P/I^nP$, by $\bar b\otimes p\mapsto bp$ modulo $I^nP$, inverse $\bar p\mapsto1\otimes p$. The scheme Zariski/etale quasi-coherent equivalence identifies these tensor and direct-image calculations with those on the etale charts. They glue, since these formulas preserve restriction and the quotient projection. Thus $j_{n,*}F_n=Q_n$, naturally in $F$. Apply lem-sfb-space-affine-cohomology to $j_n,F_n$ (which is quasi-coherent by the same chart calculation), and step 2 to obtain the canonical $A$-linear edge isomorphism $e_n:H^q(X,Q_n)\simeq H^q(X_n,F_n)$. It takes the quotient-induced cohomology map to the canonical restriction map. For $r\geq n$, the chart formula $P/I^rP\to P/I^nP$ is exactly the unit for $X_n\hookrightarrow X_r$ after tensor pullback. Consequently the canonical edge comparisons identify the transition with the quotient-induced map. For precision, the edge is the coefficient-map cohomology map of lem-sfb-ringed-site-cohomology-fmap-calculus: lem-sfb-space-affine-module-higher-image-vanishing makes $j_{n,*}$ of an injective resolution of $F_n$ a resolution of $Q_n$, and the calculus node normalizes that edge. Its composition and coefficient-naturality laws applied to the displayed chart identities prove transition compatibility and scalar compatibility. Enough injectives and terminal site models were supplied in step 2.

proof.text: Write $M=H^q(X,F)$, $D_n=H^q(X,Q_n)$, $\rho_n:M\to D_n$, and $\tau_{r,n}:D_r\to D_n$ for the quotient-induced maps, with $\tau_{r,n}\rho_r=\rho_n$. These maps are $A$-linear by functoriality with respect to scalar endomorphisms. Since multiplication by every $a\in I^n$ on $Q_n$ is zero, its induced endomorphism on $D_n$ is zero. Thus $I^nD_n=0$, and $\rho_n$ kills $I^nM$. It factors uniquely as $M\to M/I^nM\xrightarrow{\bar\theta_n}D_n$. The quotient composition identity gives compatibility of the $\bar\theta_n$ with transitions. Under $e_n$ these are precisely the $\theta_n$ in the statement.

proof.text: For each $n\geq1$, apply the long exact sequence of step 2 to $0\to G_n\to F\to Q_n\to0$. If $K_n=\ker\rho_n$ and $L_n=H^{q+1}(X,G_n)$, exactness gives $K_n=\operatorname{Im}(H^q(X,G_n)\to M)$ and $\ker\delta_n=\operatorname{Im}\rho_n$, where $\delta_n:D_n\to L_n$ is the boundary. The inclusions $G_r\subseteq G_n$, identity on $F$, and quotient $Q_r\to Q_n$ form a morphism of these short exact sequences. Naturality gives $\delta_n\tau_{r,n}=a_{r,n}\delta_r$, where $a_{r,n}:L_r\to L_n$ is induced by inclusion. This includes $q=0$, where the long exact sequence starts with zero.

proof.text: Each $L_n$ is a finite $A$-module. Indeed, step 1 makes $G_n$ coherent, and lem-sfb-space-proper-coherent-higher-images makes $R^{q+1}f_*G_n$ coherent on $\operatorname{Spec}A$. The proper map is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: its relative diagonal is a closed immersion, hence affine and quasi-compact on scheme tests. Apply lem-sfb-space-affine-base-higher-image-sections to identify $L_n$ with the sections of this coherent higher image. The affine-chart characterization in the higher-image node says those sections are $A\otimes_AN\cong N$ for a finitely generated $A$-module $N$. The conventions agree by step 2.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-space-ideal-power-cohomology-image-bound first in degree $q$, obtaining $c\geq0$. Its $n=0,m=s$ case gives $\operatorname{Im}(H^q(X,G_s)\to M)\subseteq I^{s-c}M$ for $s\geq c$. Together with steps 4 and 5 this gives $I^sM\subseteq K_s\subseteq I^{s-c}M$ whenever $s\geq\max(1,c)$. In particular $K_{n+c}\subseteq I^nM$ for every $n\geq1$. No comparison between $H^q(X,G_s)$ and $I^sM$ has been assumed: only its image in $M$ is bounded.

proof.text: Apply the same bound in degree $q+1$, obtaining $b\geq0$ such that $\operatorname{Im}(a_{n+m,n})\subseteq I^{m-b}L_n$ for every $n\geq0,m\geq b$. Fix $n\geq1$ and put $B_n=\operatorname{Im}\delta_n\subseteq L_n$. Artin-Rees applies to $B_n$ inside the finite module $L_n$ from step 6, with the given Noetherian ring $A$ and ideal $I$. It supplies $d_n\geq0$ with $I^tL_n\cap B_n\subseteq I^{t-d_n}B_n$ for $t\geq d_n$. Since $\delta_n$ is $A$-linear, $I^uB_n=\delta_n(I^uD_n)$ (expand both sides into finite sums of scalar multiples); by step 4 this is zero for $u\geq n$. Thus $I^tL_n\cap B_n=0$ for $t\geq d_n+n$.

source.place: Tags 08AY (lemma-ML-cohomology-powers-ideal), proof, and 08AZ (theorem-formal-functions), proof; Tag 08B1 (lemma-formal-functions-stalk), final paragraph, for the quotient/thickening dictionary.

proof.text: For $r\geq 2n+b+d_n$, put $m=r-n$. Then $m\geq b$ and $m-b\geq d_n+n$. The boundary identity of step 5 and step 8 show $\delta_n\tau_{r,n}(D_r)\subseteq B_n\cap I^{m-b}L_n=0$. Exactness gives $\operatorname{Im}\tau_{r,n}\subseteq\operatorname{Im}\rho_n$. The reverse inclusion holds for every $r\geq n$ because $\tau_{r,n}\rho_r=\rho_n$. We have therefore proved eventual equality of these images for each $n$, with a bound allowed to depend on $n$. No uniform Artin-Rees constant in $n$ has been claimed.

source.place: Tags 08AY (lemma-ML-cohomology-powers-ideal), proof, and 08AZ (theorem-formal-functions), proof; Tag 08B1 (lemma-formal-functions-stalk), final paragraph, for the quotient/thickening dictionary.

proof.text: Let $x=(x_n)\in\varprojlim D_n$. For fixed $n$, take $r\geq2n+b+d_n$. Compatibility and step 9 imply $x_n=\tau_{r,n}(x_r)\in\operatorname{Im}\rho_n$. For each $n\geq1$, choose a lift $u\in M$ of $x_{n+c}$ and define $y_n=u\bmod I^nM$. This is independent of the lift since $K_{n+c}\subseteq I^nM$ by step 7. If $r\geq n$ and $v$ lifts $x_{r+c}$, then $v$ also lifts $x_{n+c}$ after applying the transition, so $v-u\in K_{n+c}\subseteq I^nM$. Therefore the $y_n$ are compatible and define $\Psi(x)\in\widehat M$. The independence just proved also shows that this construction is additive and $A$-linear, by choosing sums and scalar multiples as lifts.

source.place: Tags 08AY (lemma-ML-cohomology-powers-ideal), proof, and 08AZ (theorem-formal-functions), proof; Tag 08B1 (lemma-formal-functions-stalk), final paragraph, for the quotient/thickening dictionary.

proof.text: Let $\Theta:\widehat M\to\varprojlim D_n$ have components $\bar\theta_n$. If $x\in\varprojlim D_n$ and $u$ lifts $x_{n+c}$, its class $y_n$ from step 10 maps to $\rho_n(u)=\tau_{n+c,n}(x_{n+c})=x_n$, proving $\Theta\Psi(x)=x$. Conversely, for $z=(z_n)\in\widehat M$, choose $u\in M$ representing $z_{n+c}\in M/I^{n+c}M$. It lifts the $(n+c)$-component of $\Theta(z)$, and its class modulo $I^nM$ is $z_n$ by compatibility. Step 10 then gives $\Psi\Theta(z)=z$. Thus $\Theta$ is the canonical isomorphism of limits; the displayed formulas supply both inverse identities rather than merely an abstract bijection.

source.place: Tags 08AY (lemma-ML-cohomology-powers-ideal), proof, and 08AZ (theorem-formal-functions), proof; Tag 08B1 (lemma-formal-functions-stalk), final paragraph, for the quotient/thickening dictionary.

proof.text: The limit map is $\widehat A$-linear: at level $n$, both $M/I^nM$ and $D_n$ are killed by $I^n$, and $\bar\theta_n$ is $A/I^n$-linear. Hence for $\alpha=(\alpha_n)\in\widehat A$ and $z\in\widehat M$, its $n$th component satisfies $\bar\theta_n(\alpha_nz_n)=\alpha_n\bar\theta_n(z_n)$. The same holds after $e_n$, by its scalar compatibility in step 3. For a module map $F\to F'$, functoriality takes $G_n\to G'_n$, induces $Q_n\to Q'_n$, and commutes with each quotient projection. Applying cohomology proves commutation with $\rho_n$, and their quotient factorizations commute by uniqueness. The natural edges $e_n$ then give naturality of the final comparison. Its inverse is natural because it is the inverse of this natural isomorphism; the choices in step 10 do not affect it. This proves all clauses for the prescribed infinitesimal tower without completeness, locality, or flatness assumptions.
